worked_solution:
If the maple population is $P,$ then the rate of change of the population is $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in years.

Since $75$ new maple trees are added every year, the rate of change of the population of the maples is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=75.
$$
